decisive_items: serum creatine phosphokinase was markedly elevated at over 90,000 U/L
response.rationale: R2 is the only candidate that explains the full picture: extreme CK elevation with generalized muscle tenderness and red-colored urine (without hematuria) is diagnostic of rhabdomyolysis; oliguria, hypocalcemia, and hyperphosphatemia are its renal complications. R3 captures the downstream AKI but not the muscle/CK evidence. R1 is nonspecific and cannot account for the CK elevation or pigmenturia.

rejected.why: Fever, cough, diarrhea, tachycardia, and hypotension are nonspecific; no confirmed infection source and cannot explain CK >90,000, muscle tenderness, or red urine without red cells.
